lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
A classmate's late-bus note says only that two people will be funny at the stop. Which parts must be added before this counts as a playbuilding plan?

FEEDBACK
Add beats, two different wants, and one withheld fact such as the bus arrival. Funny is not yet a stimulus plan. The page needs three ordered beats, two roles pulling different ways, and one tension choice. Withholding when the bus appears is one possible tension choice. Another is withholding why it is late, until the middle. Copying the art-room key story onto a bus stop does not count as those parts.

WATCH FOR
Renaming the house-key scene as a late bus does not create a new stimulus. A new stimulus needs its own place, problem, and people. Leaving the page blank because the group 'already improvised' also fails this lesson. Repair the plan by writing the bus problem in beats, wants, and one deliberate withhold.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Plan a late-bus scene with three beats, two different wants, and one tension choice. The stimulus is a bus that has not come. Invent the place and the two people yourself. Include ordered beats, each role's want, and exactly one fact you will withhold until the middle. Do not move the house key, the art room, or the paint bench into this plan. Add a consent line. The writing is the required evidence. Any try needs agreement and an adult nearby.

Write a short reflection naming one artistic choice you changed and why. Movement or instrument work is optional, adult-supervised and can be described instead.

teaching.rule: Make the arts idea visible: name the element, technique or performance choice you used and say what effect it creates.

teaching.feedback: Add beats, two different wants, and one withheld fact such as the bus arrival. Funny is not yet a stimulus plan. The page needs three ordered beats, two roles pulling different ways, and one tension choice. Withholding when the bus appears is one possible tension choice. Another is withholding why it is late, until the middle. Copying the art-room key story onto a bus stop does not count as those parts.

teaching.misconception: Changing the decoration without changing the artistic idea does not fix the error. Renaming the house-key scene as a late bus does not create a new stimulus. Repair the plan by writing the bus problem in beats, wants, and one deliberate withhold.

teaching.misconception: Repeating the worked example cannot show transfer to a new artwork or performance.
teaching.model: A playbuilding plan records beats, different wants, and one tension choice. This is the transfer lesson. The house-key work stays as the model. The new stimulus is a late bus, not a rename of the key. A complete plan names the stimulus, three beats in order, two roles with different wants, and one tension choice about what you withhold. It can also note a transition or a sightline, but those four parts are the minimum. The key plan below shows the shape. Your own page must be the bus. Performance stays optional. The written plan is the evidence, including a consent line: no touching, and an adult nearby if anyone tries it. Now choose a different subject or piece to show you can transfer the idea.
